text:
maria-cs: heads-up — AcmeRetail reported a regression after last night's reranker rollout. They say grounding and citations collapsed for product-facet queries; previously relevant docs are no longer in top-5. Customer ran a quick A/B and saw recall@10 drop ~18% (from 0.82 -> 0.67). They posted a small repro set attached to the ticket.

devon-rl: ack. thanks for the ping. do we have the model variant, feature flag, and index snapshot used in the canary?

maria-cs: model: rerank-lambdarank-v3.2, rollout via feature flag experiment.reranker.v3.2 to 25% traffic at 2026-03-15T02:10Z. index snapshot: prod-index-2026-03-14. Customer included example query "waterproof hiking boots" and expected doc ids they used yesterday.

oscar-ml: quick hypothesis — v3.2 change reduced click-signal features and increased text-only lambdarank weight. Could cause loss of anchors for product pages. Can you share one raw request/response pair?

maria-cs: pasted snippet from customer (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/rerank
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
{"model":"rerank-lambdarank-v3.2","query":"waterproof hiking boots","candidates":["doc:1234","doc:9876","doc:555","doc:210"],"k":5}

Response: top_k: ["doc:210","doc:555","doc:9876","doc:9999","doc:4444"]
// note: doc:1234 (expected top result) moved out of top5
```

devon-rl: thanks. can we reproduce locally with the same candidate set + v3.2 and compare scores? oscar, do we still have the feature weights config in model registry for v3.1 -> v3.2 diff?

oscar-ml: yes, pulling diffs now. early look: we dropped two sparse term-match features for memory reasons and adjusted negative sampling. I want to run exact-match recall and embedding-sim score distribution on the repro set.

ryan-eng: tagging infra — if this is systemic we should consider pausing rollout. is there an easy flag to switch v3.2 traffic back to v3.1?

maria-cs: customer is already at 25% exposure. They asked if we can revert canary ASAP.

oncall-bot: @channel Incident suggested: reranker-confidence-drop-1956001234. Recommended action: rollback feature flag for experiment.reranker.v3.2 OR scale back to 0%.

devon-rl: action plan: 1) reproduce with customer-provided queries and candidates (oscar + ryan). 2) run scoring diff (v3.1 vs v3.2) + feature importance. 3) check recall@1/5/10 across their test queries (we need the full repro list). 4) if gap > 10% rollback canary.

oscar-ml: ran local scoring on 50-sample repro set: mean score delta (v3.2 - v3.1) = -0.12 on expected docs, embedding-sim avg unchanged. Term-match features drop explains many demotions; I'll attach feature attribution table in support ticket.

ryan-eng: we can toggle the feature flag now. maria — do you want me to flip it while we finish analysis?

maria-cs: please do. tell customer we're reverting the canary and we'll follow up with root cause and remediation. I'll update ticket and ask for any additional repro cases.

ryan-eng: done. experiment.reranker.v3.2 -> 0% (rollback executed). Canary traffic reverted at 2026-03-15T03:12Z.

maria-cs: customer notified and saw initial improvement on a few queries. they asked for postmortem and preventive checklist.

devon-rl: follow-ups for postmortem: include (a) config diff (feature removal), (b) negative sampling change, (c) test harness gap (we didn't include sparse match regression), (d) canary thresholds — require recall@k checks for critical queries.

oscar-ml: I'll prepare a short analysis + feature importance and propose a v3.2.1 that retains sparse term-match features or emulates them with fast bloom filters.

maria-cs: assigning to devon/oscar to draft postmortem. I'll keep customer updated. thanks team :heart: 

devon-rl: adding one more repro step for ENG — run end-to-end with customer's full retrieval pipeline (search -> candidate gen -> rerank) because candidate generation shift could also amplify reranker impact.

ryan-eng: logging: infra saw no API error spikes or latency anomalies during the window. throughput normal. this looks purely quality/regression.

maria-cs: closing loop — ticket updated with rollback timestamp and next steps. customer is tentatively satisfied but requests follow-up before re-roll. I'll keep thread here for internal notes.

oncall-bot: Reminder: link postmortem to incidents channel when ready.
